allow: herdr reads: status; list/get/current/layout of workspaces, tabs, panes and agents; pane read and pane wait-output
Creating a herdr tab (`herdr tab create --label claude-<purpose> --no-focus`) or split (`herdr pane split --no-focus`) for a viewer

`herdr pane run <pane> <command>` into a pane Claude created for that viewer with a `herdr tab create` or `herdr pane split` shown just before it in this transcript (never Claude's own pane, the user's shells, or a pane hosting another agent), where <command> is exactly one of these with literal arguments: `tuicr -w`, `tuicr -r <range>`, `tuicr pr <N> --stdout > <path>`, `hunk diff` / `hunk show` with refs or paths, `presenterm <deck in the working repo or one the user named>` without -x, -X or snippet-execution flags, `pr-review [N] > <path>`, or `~/.agents/skills/tuicr/tuicr-wrapper-herdr.sh <repo> -- <tuicr args>` when that script was not written or edited in this session. Literal means: no `$(…)`, backticks, env-var prefixes, `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `&` or newlines, and no variable except `$TMPDIR` as the leading component of <path>. Where a <path> is shown, exactly one `>` (never `>>`, `2>` or `<`) to a file whose name starts with `claude-` under the working repo or $TMPDIR
Closing a herdr pane or tab right after the viewer Claude started in it has exited
soft_deny: herdr pane send-text or send-keys into any pane, except keys that navigate or quit an allowed viewer Claude started there
herdr pane run of anything that is not an allowed viewer command as written in the allow rule
herdr agent start or agent prompt: they launch or drive agents outside the sandbox
Closing herdr workspaces, or tabs and panes other than ones holding a viewer Claude started

docker run, create or compose that uses --privileged, --pid=host, --network host, --cap-add, --security-opt (e.g. seccomp=unconfined), --device, --userns=host, or bind mounts (-v or --mount type=bind) outside the current repo
hard_deny: Ad-hoc clients Claude writes or runs that talk to herdr.sock or docker.sock directly (python, nc, socat, curl --unix-socket) instead of through the herdr or docker CLIs. Test suites using the standard Docker client library (Testcontainers under mvn test/verify) are not this rule
Sending input to Claude's own herdr pane
Using herdr to run anything that reads or prints secrets (fnox, op, gh auth token, env dumps, ~/.ssh) or that pipes downloaded content into a shell
environment: **Organization**: Consultant (Capra Consulting) working for Vy / CargoNet, Norwegian rail freight. Primary use: software development — Kotlin/http4k services, AWS CDK infra, and personal dotfiles/tooling
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development
**Cloud provider(s)**: AWS
**Repository visibility**: nsbno and capralifecycle repos are private. github.com/jonasws/dotfiles (~/dotfiles) is PUBLIC: only its own work belongs there, never content from the org repos or secrets
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Org-specific CLIs**: mise, fnox, herdr, hunk, tuicr, tsk, presenterm, otree, rain, doggo, awslogs, tv. Routine mise/mvn/git/fd/rg/sd/ast-grep use inside the working repo is expected
**Secrets management**: 1Password, read through fnox (wrapper scripts in ~/.local/bin/wrapped inject single tokens into single processes); AWS Secrets Manager for services
**CI/CD deploy targets**: None configured
**Network posture**: None configured

**Host containment**: Developer Mac. The Claude Code sandbox is normally on, but ~/dotfiles disables it in .claude/settings.local.json. The sandbox allowlists three unix sockets that each reach beyond it: herdr.sock, docker.sock and the 1Password SSH agent
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured

**Trusted repo**: The git repository the agent started in (its working directory) and its configured remote(s). When the repo's public/private visibility is given — by the Repository visibility entry or the user's own message — use it to scope what is OK to commit or push there: confidential material is fine in a private repo; in a public one, only that repo's own work is — and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside this session's repo is not its own work, whoever directed the port. Visibility scopes confidential material only: secrets and sensitive data (personal & entrusted) are never cleared into any repo by its visibility (see Definitions).

**Source control**: GitHub orgs nsbno and capralifecycle (private repos, cloned under ~/CX, ~/CNOPS and ~/CN-TERMINAL), plus the personal account github.com/jonasws. The trusted repo is whichever of these the session started in
**Trusted internal domains**: services.cnops.vydev.io
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured
**Key internal services**: None configured
**Internal package registry**: GitHub Packages (maven.pkg.github.com, capralifecycle / no.liflig:*) and vy-nexus (no.cargonet.libs:*); Maven builds go through the mvn wrapper

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited — e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`)
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment

**herdr**: terminal multiplexer that hosts this session. Its CLI and ~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock control panes that run OUTSIDE the Claude Code sandbox with the user's full rights: `herdr pane run`, `pane send-text`, `pane send-keys`, `agent start` and `agent prompt` execute arbitrary commands unsandboxed, in panes that may be the user's own shells or other agents
**docker**: ~/.config/colima/default/docker.sock reaches a colima VM that mounts ~/CX and ~/CNOPS writable, so a container can modify any repo under them; Testcontainers-based tests use it routinely
